## Charging Infrastructure in Germany

<p class="tags"><span>Python</span><span>Pandas</span><span>GeoPandas</span><span>Streamlit</span><span>Plotly</span><span>GitHub Actions</span></p>

**Question:** How well is Germany covered with public EV charging points, and how does supply relate to the number of electric vehicles – district by district?

**What I did**

- Built a pipeline that downloads the public charging station register of the Federal Network Agency (BNetzA), reshapes it to one row per charging point and assigns each point to its district via a spatial join with BKG boundaries.
- Related the charging points to EV stock figures from the Federal Motor Transport Authority (KBA).
- Built an interactive dashboard with a district-level map and filters (e.g. state, charging type).
- Automated the monthly data refresh with GitHub Actions. Next step: moving the data to object storage with DuckDB on top, documented in an architecture decision record.

**Result:** A live, self-updating dashboard. Started as a take-home task for a data analyst position at NOW GmbH and has been extended since.

<div class="project">

## Plant Disease Recognition

<p class="tags"><span>Python</span><span>TensorFlow / Keras</span><span>Transfer Learning</span><span>Grad-CAM</span><span>SHAP</span><span>Streamlit</span></p>

**Question:** Can a model reliably tell 38 classes of healthy and diseased plant leaves apart from a single photo?

**What I did**

- Trained a CNN with transfer learning (MobileNetV2) on the Kaggle *New Plant Diseases* dataset – first with frozen weights, then fine-tuning the top layers.
- Evaluated with loss curves and confusion matrices.
- Checked *why* the model decides as it does with Grad-CAM and SHAP, to confirm it looks at leaf texture and veins rather than background artefacts.
- Packaged everything as a Streamlit app.

**Result:** A model that generalises well across all 38 classes, plus a deployed app to try it out. Capstone project of my data science bootcamp.

<div class="project">

## Credit Risk Modelling

<p class="tags"><span>Python</span><span>scikit-learn</span><span>Random Forest</span><span>Feature Engineering</span></p>

**Question:** Which loans are likely to be charged off, so that lending and investment decisions can be made with risk in mind?

**What I did**

- Worked with the LendingClub loan data (2007–2018): over 2.2 million loans with 151 features.
- Reduced it to ~418k completed loans (*Fully Paid* vs. *Charged Off*), removed identifiers and leakage-prone date fields, and dropped columns with many missing values.
- Engineered features (term, employment length, one-hot encoding, scaling).
- Trained a class-balanced Random Forest on a stratified 70/30 split and evaluated precision, recall and ROC AUC per class.

**Result:** A reproducible end-to-end baseline (notebooks, scripts, saved model) that flags risky loans well and can be extended with gradient boosting.

<p class="links">
<a href="https://github.com/FelixSchramm/credit-risk-modelling" target="_blank">Code on GitHub</a>
